questions.question:
Which of the following best identifies the grammatical role of the phrase "in its pursuit of knowledge" in the sentence:**

"Consciousness, in its pursuit of knowledge**, initially assumes that its object is something external and independent."

options.text: Noun phrase functioning as the subject

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**in its pursuit of knowledge**" functions as an **adverbial phrase** because it modifies the main verb "**assumes**."
 
• It describes the **circumstances or the context** under which the consciousness perform the action of assuming.
 
• Adverbial phrases of this type often answer the questions "when," "why," or "under what conditions" an action takes place.
 
• The phrase is set off by commas as a parenthetical adverbial, which provides additional information about the timing and motivation of the verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Sentence Breakdown:** *"Consciousness [Subject], **in its pursuit of knowledge [Adverbial Phrase]**, initially [Adverb] **assumes [Verb]** that its object is something external and independent."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Adjective modifying "Consciousness"** – An adjective would describe a quality of the noun (e.g., "The *curious* consciousness"). This phrase describes the process of the action instead.
 
• **Option 3: Noun phrase functioning as the subject** – The subject of the sentence is the single noun "Consciousness."
 
• **Option 4: Appositive explaining "object"** – An appositive would follow the word "object" to rename or define it (e.g., "its object, *the external world*"). This phrase appears much earlier in the sentence.

questions.question:
In the clause:

“...believing itself to have attained certainty,”

What grammatical structure is “believing” a part of?

options.text: A finite verb in past tense

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**believing**" is a **present participle** (the -ing form of a verb used as an adjective).
 
• In the phrase "**believing itself to have attained certainty**," it functions as a **participial phrase** that modifies the noun phrase "each stage of consciousness."
 
• A participial phrase acts as an **adjectival modifier**, providing extra information about the subject without functioning as the main finite verb of the sentence.
 
• It is non-finite, meaning it does not show tense or person on its own and requires a main verb ("encounters") to complete the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Structural Breakdown:** *"...each stage of consciousness [Noun Phrase], **believing itself to have attained certainty [Participial Phrase modifying the noun phrase]**, encounters [Main Verb] its own inadequacy."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: A relative clause** – A relative clause typically begins with a relative pronoun like "which" or "that" (e.g., "which believes itself...").
 
• **Option 2: A passive voice** – Passive voice would require the past participle and a form of the verb 'to be' (e.g., "is believed"). "Believing" is in the active form.
 
• **Option 4: A finite verb in past tense** – A finite verb functions as the main verb of a clause and shows tense. The past tense of believe is "believed." "Believing" is a non-finite form.

questions.question:
What is the best synonym for the word **“sublated”** in the context:

“...the apparent duality of subject and object is thus sublated in the dialectic...”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. preserved and transformed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"sublated"** in the context of philosophy, particularly in Hegelian dialectics, means:

 
 
• The process by which contradictions are overcome and preserved by being transformed into a higher unity. (संकलित और रूपांतरित किया गया)
 
 
 
• In the sentence provided, "...the apparent duality of subject and object is thus sublated in the dialectic...," "sublated" implies that the duality is both preserved and transformed within the dialectical process.
 
• **Preserved and transformed** means maintaining the essential aspects while also changing them into a higher form of unity or understanding.
 
• **Example:** The contradictions of the previous argument were sublated into a greater synthesis.

Therefore, the best synonym for "sublated" in the given context is: **preserved and transformed.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Removed** (हटाया गया): Taken away or gotten rid of.

 
 
• **Example:** The stains were removed from the fabric.
 
 
 
• **Repressed** (दबाया गया): Restrained or suppressed.
 
 
• **Example:** The emotions were repressed to prevent conflict.
 
 
 
• **Ignored** (अनदेखा किया गया): Paid no attention to.
 
 
• **Example:** The warning signs were ignored by the workers.

questions.question: What paradox does Hegel highlight through the master-slave dialectic?

options.text: That true knowledge comes from dominance over others
That the slave remains forever inferior in self-awareness
That the master loses recognition by denying the slave's autonomy
That consciousness cannot exist without subjugation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paradox Hegel describes is rooted in the **need for recognition**. A self-conscious being needs to be recognized by another self-conscious being to confirm its own existence and freedom.
 
• The master attempts to gain this recognition by **subjugating the slave**, turning them into a mere instrument or object.
 
• Because the master now views the slave as an **inferior object** rather than an independent subject, the recognition the master receives is hollow and "unrealized."
 
• Ultimately, the master becomes **dependent** on the slave’s labor, while the slave, through the "negation" of the material world in labor, achieves a higher level of independent self-awareness.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Relevant Text Quote:** *"The master, in reducing the slave to a mere instrument, **deprives himself of a fully realized recognition**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: True knowledge comes from dominance** – The text argues the opposite: dominance leads to an "inadequacy" of consciousness and a loss of true recognition.
 
• **Option 2: The slave remains forever inferior** – Hegel suggests the slave actually attains a "deeper awareness of autonomy" through labor, potentially surpassing the master's self-awareness.
 
• **Option 4: Consciousness cannot exist without subjugation** – While the dialectic involves a struggle, the goal is "sublation" and the discovery of a mediated truth, not the permanent necessity of one person enslaving another.

questions.question: What term describes: "The view that all human knowledge and experience are shaped by the limitations of the human mind, and thus we cannot know things as they truly are."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Kantianism"** refers to the philosophical viewpoint proposed by Immanuel Kant, which emphasizes that human knowledge and experience are shaped by the inherent limitations of the human mind and perception. It asserts that we cannot truly know things as they are but only as they appear to us. (कांटवाद)
 
 
• **Example:** According to Kantianism, our understanding of the universe is limited to phenomena shaped by our perception, rather than the universe as it exists independently.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The CEO (1)/ called off (2)/ the meeting (3)/ without giving any reason out. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in **Part 4** of the sentence: **"without giving any reason out."**
 
• **Reason for Error:** The addition of the word **"out"** after "giving any reason" is grammatically incorrect and redundant.
 
• **Usage of 'Give':** To "give a reason" means to provide or state a justification. The verb "give" does not require the particle "out" when used in this context.
 
• **Phrasal Verb 'Give out':** The phrasal verb **"give out"** has specific meanings that do not fit here: 
 
 
• To distribute something (e.g., "She gave out the flyers").
 
• To stop working/fail (e.g., "His legs gave out after the race").
 
• To emit (e.g., "The heater gives out a lot of warmth").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The CEO called off the meeting without giving any reason."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Called off:** This is a correct phrasal verb meaning **to cancel**. (e.g., The match was called off due to rain).
 
• **Part 1, 2, and 3:** These parts are grammatically sound. "The CEO" (subject), "called off" (verb), and "the meeting" (object) form a clear and correct clause.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The team leader called up (1)/ each employee separately (2)/ but failed to bring on (3)/ their actual grievances. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
Shutterstock

__
 
• The error lies in **Part 3** of the sentence: **"but failed to bring on."**
 
• **Reason for Error:** The phrasal verb **"bring on"** is used incorrectly here. "Bring on" typically means to cause something (usually something unpleasant) to happen or develop, such as an illness or a challenge (e.g., "The cold weather brought on his cough").
 
• **Correct Phrasal Verb:** The intended meaning is to elicit, reveal, or make something manifest. The correct phrasal verb should be **"bring out"** or **"bring up"**. 
 
 
• **Bring out:** To make something apparent or to elicit a quality/reaction (e.g., "The leader failed to bring out their grievances").
 
• **Bring up:** To mention or introduce a topic for discussion.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The team leader called up each employee separately but failed to **bring out** their actual grievances."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Called up (Part 1):** This is a correct phrasal verb meaning to telephone someone or to summon them for a specific purpose.
 
• **Separately (Part 2):** This adverb correctly modifies the action of calling the employees individually.
 
• **Grievances (Part 4):** This noun refers to real or imagined wrongs or other causes for complaint or protest, which fits the professional context of the sentence.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:

Of all the analysts on the panel, Priya was considered the ___ in macroeconomic interpretation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**best**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**best**" is the superlative form of the adjective "**good**."
 
• We use the superlative degree when comparing one person or thing against a group of three or more. The phrase "**Of all the analysts**" indicates a group comparison.
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and 4 are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Of all the analysts on the panel, Priya was considered the **best**__ in macroeconomic interpretation."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "better"** is the comparative degree, used for comparing only two people or things.
 
• **Option 3: "most better"** is incorrect because "better" is already comparative; adding "most" creates an ungrammatical double comparison.
 
• **Option 4: "more best"** is incorrect because "best" is already superlative; adding "more" is redundant and ungrammatical.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the underlined part of the sentence:

She sings __as better as__ a trained vocalist.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**as well as**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The construction **"as...as"** is used to show that two things are equal in some way.
 
• In this structure, we must use the **positive degree** of the adjective or adverb (e.g., "well," not "better").
 
• Since the word modifies the verb **"sings,"** the adverb **"well"** is the grammatically correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"She sings **as well as**__ a trained vocalist."*

questions.question:
Change the following from active to passive:

Industry leaders have been challenging the proposed legislation for its lack of clarity and enforcement mechanisms.

options.text: The proposed legislation has been being challenged for its lack of clarity and enforcement mechanisms by industry leaders.
The proposed legislation was challenged by industry leaders for clarity and mechanism.
The legislation has been challenged by leaders for its lack of clarity.
The legislation is being challenged by industry leaders for its lack of clarity.

questions.solution:

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Industry leaders have been challenging the proposed legislation for its lack of clarity and enforcement mechanisms."
 
• The tense used here is **Present Perfect Continuous** (have been challenging).
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "The proposed legislation" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "have been challenging" to "has been being challenged" (present perfect continuous passive structure: *has/have + been + being + past participle*).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "industry leaders."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The proposed legislation has been being challenged for its lack of clarity and enforcement mechanisms by industry leaders."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The proposed legislation was challenged..." – Incorrect tense (Simple Past passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"The legislation has been challenged..." – Incorrect tense (Present Perfect passive) and omits parts of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"The legislation is being challenged..." – Incorrect tense (Present Continuous passive).

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a meaningful passage.
1. The team submitted the compiled data to the analytics division.
2. Raw survey responses were extracted from multiple sources.
3. Each dataset underwent preprocessing and standardization.
4. Redundant entries were eliminated using automated filters.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentences describe the workflow of data processing from raw survey responses to submission to the analytics division.
 
• **Sentence 2** is the starting point because it introduces the extraction of raw survey responses:
 
 
• "Raw survey responses were extracted from multiple sources."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3** comes next as it describes preprocessing and standardization of the extracted data:
 
 
• "Each dataset underwent preprocessing and standardization."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4** follows as it discusses the elimination of redundant entries, which logically comes after preprocessing:
 
 
• "Redundant entries were eliminated using automated filters."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1** is the final step as it describes the submission of the processed data to the analytics division:
 
 
• "The team submitted the compiled data to the analytics division."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **2-3-4-1**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:**

"Raw survey responses were extracted from multiple sources. Each dataset underwent preprocessing and standardization. Redundant entries were eliminated using automated filters. The team submitted the compiled data to the analytics division."</div
